# FDGA040

> DO NOT use `this.` unless absolutely necessary.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section A.1.6 Other.

This is a coding style convention. The book treats the appendix A conventions as suggestions, so you can override it.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

IDE0003, which reports 'this.', is not part of the SDK's code style analyzers.

## Options

```ini
dotnet_style_qualification_for_field = false
dotnet_style_qualification_for_property = false
dotnet_style_qualification_for_method = false
dotnet_style_qualification_for_event = false
```

## From the book

If the private members are named correctly, a “`this.`” should not be required except to invoke an extension method. The use of the underscore prefix on fields already provides a distinction between field access and variable access.
